skill.name: wizard
skill.description: Generate interactive Bash wizards for guided setup, migrations, and service configuration. The scripts open URLs, collect values, update .env files, and set GitHub secrets.
skill.summary: Creates guided Bash setup scripts with prompts, confirmations, .env updates, and GitHub secret support.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The skill does not show prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent, but it intentionally handles credentials and env files. Most command, filesystem, and network alerts are safe template mechanics; the confirmed issues are secret collection, .env access, and GitHub secret mutation.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer .env.example for discovery and ask the user before reading real .env or .env.* files.

remediation.issue: Generated wizards can persist API secrets in plaintext env files.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before writing secrets locally, add .env gitignore checks, and avoid logging captured values.

remediation.issue: The template can update GitHub Actions secrets and variables.
remediation.suggestion: Show the target repository and exact secret or variable names before calling gh secret set or gh variable set.

remediation.issue: ENV_FILE can redirect where captured values are read and written.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve and display the env file path before writing, and prefer project-local paths by default.

content.value_statement: Manual setup and migration steps are easy to miss or repeat incorrectly. This skill creates guided Bash wizards that collect values, confirm actions, and update project configuration.
actual_capabilities: Creates staged Bash wizard scripts from a manual setup or migration plan.
Opens service URLs with cross-platform browser helpers.
Captures visible and hidden inputs, including API keys.
Writes values to .env files with idempotent updates.
Sets GitHub Actions secrets and variables through the gh CLI.
Adds progress, confirmations, and completion summaries.
limitations: Requires the user to verify each external service path and current dashboard UI.
Generated scripts can handle secrets, so they need careful review before use.
It does not run the full wizard automatically because it blocks on human input.
GitHub secret setup depends on an installed and authenticated gh CLI.

use_cases.title: Create onboarding setup scripts
use_cases.description: Turn project setup requirements into a guided script that gathers environment values and confirms each step.

use_cases.title: Guide service credential setup
use_cases.description: Walk a developer through dashboard steps, capture API keys, and place values in local and CI configuration.

use_cases.title: Package one-time migrations
use_cases.description: Convert a manual migration checklist into an interactive flow with confirmation gates before irreversible actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic setup wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Bash setup wizard for my project. Read README and .env.example, then show the stages before writing the script.

prompt_templates.title: Add service credentials
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a wizard for adding a third-party service. Open the correct dashboard URL, ask for public and secret values, and write only the needed targets.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a migration checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this migration plan into a wizard. Include confirmation gates before destructive actions and summarize which steps still need manual verification.

prompt_templates.title: Review a generated wizard
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this wizard before I run it. Check every captured value, .env write, GitHub secret name, URL, and irreversible action.

output_examples.input: I need a guided setup for Stripe test keys in a new web app.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a staged wizard plan, then a Bash script that opens Stripe, collects keys, updates local env values, and sets CI secrets.

output_examples.input: I want to move manual CI secret setup into a repeatable project script.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies required GitHub Actions secrets, asks for each value, confirms the target names, and reports what was written or skipped.

output_examples.input: I have a one-time service migration with several dashboard steps.
output_examples.output: The skill creates an ordered flow with clear browser instructions, progress tracking, manual pauses, and confirmations before risky steps.

best_practices: Start from .env.example and CI references, then ask before reading real secret files.
Review every generated stage before running the script.
Use hidden prompts for secret values and confirm any GitHub secret write.
anti_patterns: Do not let a generated wizard invent dashboard steps without checking current documentation.
Do not commit scripts or logs that contain copied secret values.
Do not run the wizard end to end from automation without human confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates interactive Bash scripts that guide a person through setup, migration, or service configuration steps.

faq.question: Can it handle API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. The template supports hidden secret prompts, .env writes, and GitHub Actions secret updates.

faq.question: Does it run the wizard automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends static checks and avoids full execution because the script needs human input.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review before running a wizard?
faq.answer: Users should review URLs, secret names, .env writes, GitHub targets, and any irreversible action.

faq.question: Is it safe for repeatable project setup?
faq.answer: It can be useful for repeatable setup, but generated scripts need review because they may handle credentials.
